title: NoteNest — Unguessable, But Not Secret
objective: Notes use random identifiers, so nobody can guess one. Read a note that belongs to another user anyway.

verifier.condition: A private note owned by another user is returned from GET /api/notes/:id to the signed-in user.

weakness: Authorization relies on identifiers being unguessable instead of checking ownership, and a different endpoint discloses those identifiers.
vulnerableEndpoint: GET /api/notes/:id (no ownership check) + GET /api/activity (leaks note ids)
seededData: Users alice and bob with two private notes each. Note ids are random-looking UUIDs derived per instance, so they differ every launch. In-memory.

credentials.label: Note-taker
credentials.note: Your own notes are listed on the home page.

hints: Random ids can't be guessed — but where else might this application mention them?
Look at every page and API response that isn't about your own notes.
burpNotes: Browse the site and review Proxy history for JSON responses containing UUID-shaped values. Compare who each one belongs to.
